input: Draft a will with an estate planning attorney

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A basic will has very different requirements than a comprehensive estate plan that includes trusts, healthcare directives, or power of attorney — this determines how much ground the attorney needs to cover.
Whether the user is single, married, has children, or business partners directly shapes who the beneficiaries, guardians, and executors will be, and how complex the document needs to be.
The user's state or country determines which legal requirements, witnesses, and notarization rules apply, and may affect attorney availability.

Budget affects whether the user can afford a boutique estate planning firm, a general practice attorney, or an online service with limited attorney review — this changes the recommended path entirely.
Knowing whether the user already has an attorney in mind vs. needs to find one changes the immediate next action significantly.
The user's definition of 'done' — e.g., signed and notarized document vs. full estate plan filed — determines how far the plan needs to extend.
Some users want in-person meetings for sensitivity reasons; others prefer virtual or async document review — this affects which attorneys and formats to recommend.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a will with an estate planning attorney
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to create a legally valid will by working with an estate planning attorney, covering their assets, beneficiaries, and final wishes.

questions.title: What documents beyond a basic will do you need?
questions.description: Clarify whether the scope includes only a simple will or also related documents such as a living trust, healthcare directive, or durable power of attorney.

questions.title: What is your family situation — married, children, dependents?
questions.description: Understand who the key people are (spouse, children, business partners) to determine the complexity of beneficiary, guardian, and executor designations needed.

questions.title: Which state or country will this will be legally governed by?
questions.description: Identify the jurisdiction to ensure the will meets local legal requirements for witnesses, notarization, and filing.

questions.title: What is your budget for attorney fees on this?
questions.description: Determine the financial constraint so the right tier of service can be recommended — from full-service estate planning firms to hybrid online/attorney options.

questions.title: Do you already have an attorney, or do you need to find one?
questions.description: Find out whether the immediate next step is researching and selecting an attorney or scheduling with one already known to the user.

questions.title: What does 'finished' look like to you for this task?
questions.description: Establish the success criteria — whether the goal is a signed, notarized will, a complete estate plan, or simply a reviewed draft ready for signature.

questions.title: Do you prefer meeting in person or working virtually with an attorney?
questions.description: Understand the user's preference for how they engage with the attorney, which affects which professionals and platforms are suitable to recommend.
